data.body:
Landed and closed. Gerrit change **3126** merged — `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1` (CI run 40756956262), 0 unresolved comments, submitted revision-scoped against `6ee09e31cd06f639bae960ebe4dc780d4b819245`. That commit is now an ancestor of `gerrit/main`; the GitHub mirror was still catching up at close time.

Closed `env_integration` — an upstream packaging defect (pypandoc#447) repaired at bootstrap rather than a rebar logic error.

Operational note for the next session hitting this: a gated close over MCP timed out twice at the client's 60s deadline with no verdict. The completion verifier itself passes — run via `verify_completion_start` it returned PASS with a certified attestation at `verified_at_sha` matching the merged commit. The close still re-ran the gate because `ref` defaults to the MCP server's own HEAD, which did not contain the commit, so the fresh signature was not current for the ref being closed against. Passing `ref=<the merged sha>` to `transition_ticket` made the existing signature current and the close returned immediately. Worth preferring `ref` explicitly whenever the work was committed somewhere other than the server's checkout.
